signal: nOps now processes over $2B in cloud spend, was named #1 by G2 in cloud cost management, and is scaling its FinOps platform after a $30M Series A

email.body1:
John, saw nOps cross $2B in cloud spend under management and take the #1 G2 spot in cloud cost management.

That kind of category lead usually pulls in more in-market accounts than the team can cover before they cool, especially as AI workloads push cloud bills up. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for nOps off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
John, quick follow-up for nOps.

As a CRO, you know board expectations on pipeline usually climb faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to hit the number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings nOps needs across FinOps accounts this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
John, last bit of proof for nOps.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how nOps' reply rate likely compares to other Series-A startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
John, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Running revenue at a category leader is busy enough.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a FinOps motion? I'll tailor it to nOps either way.
